findings.title: Model deserialization executes code on load (pickle backdoor)
findings.description: The pickle stream imports dangerous callables and invokes them via a reduce/build step. Loading this model runs attacker code.
findings.impact: Full remote code execution on any machine that loads the model — a classic distributed-ML supply-chain backdoor.
findings.remediation: Do not unpickle untrusted models. Convert to safetensors; load PyTorch with weights_only=True; verify provenance and a signed checksum before use.

findings.title: torch.load without weights_only=True
findings.description: torch.load unpickles by default and will execute code embedded in a malicious checkpoint.
findings.impact: A poisoned checkpoint runs arbitrary code on every node that loads it.
findings.remediation: Pass weights_only=True (PyTorch >=2.0) or load safetensors; verify checksums of shared weights.

findings.title: HuggingFace trust_remote_code=True
findings.description: Loading a model/dataset with trust_remote_code=True runs arbitrary code shipped in the repo.
findings.impact: A malicious model repo executes code on your training nodes.
findings.remediation: Set trust_remote_code=False; if custom code is required, vendor and review it, and pin the revision.

findings.title: Unsafe deserialization: yaml.load (unsafe)
findings.description: yaml.load (unsafe) deserializes data that may execute code.
findings.impact: Code execution if the input is attacker-influenced.

findings.title: Federated aggregation without robust/backdoor defenses
findings.description: Distributed/federated training averages client updates with no robust aggregation, update clipping, or differential privacy — the standard defenses against model-poisoning / backdoor attacks.
findings.evidence: federated markers present; no robust-aggregation keyword found
findings.impact: A few malicious clients can implant a backdoor (targeted misclassification on a trigger) via poisoned updates.
findings.remediation: Use robust aggregation (Krum / Multi-Krum, trimmed-mean, median, Bulyan), clip client update norms, add differential privacy, and monitor updates for anomalies. Post-train, screen with Neural Cleanse / STRIP / activation clustering.
findings.poc:
# e.g. replace FedAvg with trimmed-mean + norm clipping
# agg = trimmed_mean(updates, beta=0.1)
# updates = [clip_norm(u, max_norm) for u in updates]
